# Trayo GTM UI — copy these files into your project

You are likely a coding agent building a go-to-market application on the Trayo
API. Use this library for the UI. It makes the app look like Trayo, and it
handles the two things a GTM app renders constantly — people and companies —
including their avatars and logos.

Presentational React components only. No server-side logic, no data fetching.

## IMPORTANT: copy the files in. Do not install from this URL.

This URL is a **temporary delivery mechanism** and will stop working. Your job
is to copy the source into the application you are building so the app keeps
working forever with no dependency on this host.

Do NOT run `npm install <this-url>/something.tgz`. That writes this temporary
URL into package.json as a dependency spec, and every future install, every CI
run, and every fresh clone breaks the moment this host goes away.

## Step 1 — vendor the source

From your project root:

    mkdir -p src/trayo-ui
    curl -L <BASE_URL>/trayo-ui.tar.gz | tar xz -C src --strip-components=0

That gives you `src/trayo-ui/` containing `index.ts`, `components/`, `lib/`,
`styles/` (with the Polymath woff2 files) and a copy of README.md + AGENTS.md.

Put it wherever your project keeps source. `src/trayo-ui/` is the assumed
location below; adjust the import paths if you choose another.

Can't run curl? Fetch `<BASE_URL>/src/` and walk the tree — every file is
readable individually, e.g. `<BASE_URL>/src/components/person.tsx`. The
manifest at `<BASE_URL>/files.txt` lists every path.

## Step 2 — install the real npm dependencies

These are ordinary public packages and are permanent:

    npm install react react-dom clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react \
      class-variance-authority tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite \
      @radix-ui/react-avatar @radix-ui/react-checkbox @radix-ui/react-dialog \
      @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu @radix-ui/react-label @radix-ui/react-popover \
      @radix-ui/react-progress @radix-ui/react-scroll-area @radix-ui/react-select \
      @radix-ui/react-separator @radix-ui/react-slot @radix-ui/react-switch \
      @radix-ui/react-tabs @radix-ui/react-tooltip

Requires Tailwind CSS v4 and React 18 or 19.

## Step 3 — wire up the CSS

In your CSS entry, in this order:

    @import "tailwindcss";
    @import "./trayo-ui/styles/trayo-ui.css";

No `@source` line is needed — the components now live inside your own source
tree, which Tailwind v4 already scans. If your CSS entry is not a sibling of
`trayo-ui/`, fix the relative path accordingly.

## Step 4 — use it

    import { AppShell, PageContainer, PageHeader, Person, CompanyCard, Button } from './trayo-ui'

    export default function App() {
      return (
        <AppShell>
          <PageContainer>
            <PageHeader title="Target accounts" actions={<Button>Import</Button>} />
            <CompanyCard company={{ name: 'Ramp', domain: 'ramp.com', industry: 'Fintech' }} />
            <Person person={{ id: 'p-1', name: 'Dana Whitfield', title: 'VP RevOps',
                              company: 'Ramp', companyDomain: 'ramp.com' }} />
          </PageContainer>
        </AppShell>
      )
    }

Read `src/trayo-ui/README.md` (now in your repo) for the full component surface.

## What still points at the network, and why that is fine

Two things resolve images from Trayo production — NOT from this temporary host,
so they keep working:

- company logos → `https://api.trayo.ai/api/brand-image?domain=…` (public, no key)
- the 50 fallback faces → `https://app.trayo.ai/images/placeholder/NN.png`

To self-host the faces instead, grab `<BASE_URL>/placeholder-faces.tar.gz`,
drop the PNGs in your static directory, and set the base:

    <TrayoUIProvider placeholderFaceBase="/images/placeholder">

## The rules that matter

1. Rendering a person? Use <Person> or <PersonCard>. Never hand-assemble an
   avatar and a name. A person always gets a face — the real photo, else one of
   50 built-in illustrated fallbacks keyed off the person id. Never initials.
2. Rendering a company? Use <Company> or <CompanyCard>. Pass `domain` and the
   logo resolves itself. Never hand-write a logo <img> or an initials tile.
3. Wrap the app in <AppShell>. Without it the page reads as generic Tailwind.
4. Use the provided components before writing your own.
5. No raw colours. Not #hex, not rgb(), not bg-slate-800 or text-blue-400.
   Use bg-surface-card, text-text-secondary, border-border-subtle,
   bg-accent-brand, text-success-text. They handle light and dark themselves.
6. Content uses type roles (text-page-title, text-name, text-body, text-meta,
   text-eyebrow). Controls use the Tailwind scale (text-sm font-medium).
   Never text-[15px].
7. <Button loading> — do not swap in your own spinner.
8. Use cn() from ./trayo-ui, not bare clsx.

## API shapes map straight through

`PersonLike` and `CompanyLike` are loose supersets of GET /v1/people and
GET /v1/accounts rows. Pass the API object directly; everything but `name` is
optional and missing fields simply do not render.

    const { data } = await fetch('/v1/people?limit=25').then(r => r.json())
    return data.map(p => <Person key={p.id} person={p} showContact />)
